passes.definition: Architecture and centralized configuration; repo scope. Layering, dependency cycles, boundaries, dead modules, central settings and reusable libraries.
current_verified_facts: First-party Python packages separate canonical offline backtesting, research runtime, Bot Manager, Oracle and ecosystem. Exact first-party package pins establish explicit dependency boundaries. Executor and retired liquidity keep their own packages and environments.

Architecture documents distinguish offline evidence, disarmed live-capable extension, explicitly gated Oracle webhook execution, retired liquidity, and isolated public website/D1/Stripe. The website has inactive saved bot definitions and no per-user execution worker. This review does not establish hosted/local execution parity.

Extension has a shared command registry and declared DEFAULT_CONFIG/getConfig/setConfig boundary. SolTUI has an importable command surface, Settings dataclass and shared settings API; Bot Manager has typed immutable defaults. No evidence found that every UI is wholly blocked from all mandatory settings.

Reusable functions live in importable equivalent package paths; a literal universal lib directory is unnecessary. Independent exposure and resting-grid simulation engines have documented distinct semantics and are not automatically a duplication defect.

findings.trigger: Deployment and read-tuning parameters remain spread across component modules rather than one exported component settings schema.
evidence: soltui/compound.py:75-84 public endpoints, headline feeds, LIVE_BARS, ADAPTIVE_LIVE_BARS, HTTP_TIMEOUT
soltui/jupiter_tokens.py:13-15 public API and response cap
findings.action: Inventory changeable deployment/read-tuning parameters and define typed per-component settings access with safe validation. Preserve code-enforced money/security caps; do not make them freely editable to satisfy centralization.

findings.trigger: Bootstrap standards call for a common operations registry, safe error schema/remediation map and generated per-operation help; current component-specific implementations do not complete that repo-wide contract.
findings.action: Design and populate the common operation/error metadata from existing component registries. Preserve fixed redacted public errors and no automatic retry of ambiguous financial writes. Generic retry infrastructure would violate venue reconciliation rules.

limits: No fresh exhaustive import-graph/cycle/dead-module proof was run in this read-only row. Full semantic per-file coverage is recorded separately by component reviewers.
Documented architectural debt prevents a blanket M3 CLEAN. Repo-wide centralization and settings UI are not implemented by this assessment.

passes.definition: Dependency and supply chain; repo scope. Outdated/known-vulnerable dependencies, unused dependencies and license flags.
current_verified_facts: Current isolated environment metadata compatibility check completed exit0 for85 packages. It does not query vulnerability advisories, establish latest versions, prove loaded source identity or identify unused packages.

Current Dependabot configuration covers GitHub Actions, six pip components, two uv components and website npm. Earlier missing-coverage findings are superseded. Extension declares no npm runtime/dev dependency tree.

Website has exact dev dependency versions and a v3 package lock. Executor/liquidity uv lockfiles exist. CI actions use commit SHAs. These facts reduce resolution ambiguity but do not prove complete transitive security/license acceptance.

Parent completed current pip-audit2.10.1 exit0; independently parsed result has85 distributions,79 publicly auditable and0 listed vulnerabilities. Six first-party packages were skipped with older installed distribution metadata. Their source review remains independent of PyPI advisory lookup.

Extension npm audit exited1 ENOLOCK; extension has no runtime/dev dependency graph to audit. ENOLOCK is retained as a nonzero attempted check, not counted as an audit pass.

findings.trigger: SolTUI installation can resolve a different private supervisor implementation on a later installation because the Git requirement lacks a commit/ref.
findings.action: Resolve a reviewed immutable commit and pin it in the supported installer/lock flow; qualify the relevant native lifecycle tests. No Git fetch/install was performed here.

findings.trigger: The broad root requirements freeze conflicts with current supported component constraints if treated as their installer: numpy2.5.3 vs>=2.5.4; mcp2.3.0 vs1.30.0; solders0.29.0 vs<0.28; cryptography50.0.1 vs50.0.2.
findings.action: Mark the root file as a dated environment export or replace it with a deliberate supported aggregate lock. Existing README/installation examples read in this task use component-scoped files; no current installed incompatibility is claimed.

findings.trigger: Current public Python and website dependency advisory checks pass within their stated package scopes, but skipped private packages, separate native environment lock resolution, unused dependencies, outdated versions and transitive licenses remain outside those checks.
evidence: /tmp/oraclebot-python-audit-current-20261112.json:85 distributions,79 publicly auditable,0 listed vulnerabilities,6 first-party skips
findings.action: Retain completed current advisory results and actual exits. Separately assess unused dependencies, release freshness, license obligations and any additional native-environment resolutions. Do not create an empty extension dependency graph merely to hide ENOLOCK.

findings.trigger: Liquidity CI runs uv sync without --frozen, while Executor CI enforces its lock. A changed manifest can silently re-resolve the liquidity dependency set during CI.
findings.action: Make supported lock consistency explicit after a qualified lock update. The existing lock was not re-resolved or claimed current by this review.

passes.definition: Tooling gaps; repo scope. Linter config, JS type checking, CI, test runner, formatter, pre-commit and pinning.
current_verified_facts: CI and test runners exist: Python unittest/pytest, node:test, extension browser dry runs, website Playwright, documentation/provenance checks, isolated installed package checks, and four optional timed SolTUI shards. It would be false to report absent CI or absent runners.

Executor/liquidity have committed Ruff configuration and formatting checks. Other Python jobs install/run Ruff but no root pyproject/ruff.toml/.ruff.toml was found; current direct SolTUI Ruff settings resolve to tool defaults.

A repository pre-commit script exists and rebuilds/stages offline indexes plus runs backtester tests. Current worktree core.hooksPath query returned exit1 with no configured value; actual hook activation is unproven. The hook was read as data and never executed in this task.

findings.trigger: Non-Executor/liquidity Python lint policy depends on tool defaults, and ecosystem/Oracle CI installs unpinned ruff. Changing the tool version can change required diagnostics.
evidence: No root Ruff config paths at current observation
findings.action: Commit an explicit compatible shared Ruff configuration and pin the CI tool version; adopt only after baselining existing Low/style debt. This assessment does not authorize broad style-only churn.

findings.trigger: The read npm scripts/CI provide syntax checks and behavioral tests, but no committed JavaScript type checker or JS linter configuration was identified.
findings.action: Choose a bounded checkJs/JSDoc or equivalent checked-interface adoption for risky shared APIs and configure a deterministic JS lint policy. Do not claim node --check establishes type safety.

findings.trigger: Mutable private Git HEAD, broad component version floors and nonfrozen liquidity resolution prevent a universal reproducible toolchain claim.
findings.action: Define supported reproducible development/CI dependency sets. Up-to-date floors are not an immutable lock.

findings.trigger: The committed hook script exists but this worktree has no observed core.hooksPath setting.
findings.action: Parent/root should use the documented setup or explicit gates when delivering. Do not activate/execute an index-writing hook inside this read-only assessment.

passes.definition: Test-suite performance; applicable here to repo test execution. Faster same coverage/behavior, safe parallel eligibility, isolation of global mutable state, no removed tests/assertion merges/mutated-setup hoists.
current_verified_facts: scripts/soltui_ci.py rejects failed/empty discovery and duplicate IDs, sorts individual cases, partitions tests[shard::shards], and prints20 slowest durations. Existing full CI uses four independent runners, not unsafe shared-thread parallelism.

SolTUI test package replaces nine inherited owner directories before module imports. Per-case contexts remain necessary for module globals, settings, registries, environment patches and lifecycle state. This isolation protects owner files but does not automatically stub every HTTP/service boundary.

The shared offline_console_reads fixture supplies a fixed product catalogue and unloaded service status. Existing guarded root and independent cohorts established zero denied external/process attempts only within their stated process-local scope. No production permission was weakened to make tests pass.

findings.trigger: Many UI/lifecycle tests mutate module-level settings, environment, registry/client mocks, process leases and asynchronous state; full thread-parallel or setup-hoisting equivalence is not proven.
evidence: Historical guard failures caught swallowed outbound/service attempts despite assertions passing.
findings.action: Retain process-separated shards; classify and prove independent cohorts before additional parallelism. Prefer isolated temporary roots/owned fixtures. Do not remove tests, merge distinct assertions or hoist setup any test mutates.

findings.trigger: Historical headless cohorts take minutes while synthetic unit cohorts take seconds to about one minute. These unequal scopes do not establish an equal-coverage speedup.
findings.action: Use existing per-test duration output to target deterministic waits/fixture construction. Fake timers only where lifecycle/lease/event equivalence is statically proven; preserve actual process and cancellation acceptance boundaries.
